paragraph: Angola's law is [Law no. 11/02 of 16 August 2002, the Law on Access to Administrative Documents](<https://angolex.com/paginas/leis/lei-de-acesso-aos-documentos-administrativos-11a-02a.html>). It gives a right to ask public bodies for the documents they hold. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a decree, regulation or order made under the law, or says its oversight body is set up. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law, or an information commission or commissioner set up, or an existing body taking up the oversight.

[The Council of Ministers of Burundi adopted a draft law on access to public information on 10 June 2026](<https://mincom.gov.bi/le-conseil-des-ministres-adopte-le-projet-de-loi-portant-acces-a-linformation-publique/>). The ministry described a legal vacuum on the subject. In the last twelve months, [the National Assembly adopted the bill unanimously on 10 September 2026](<https://www.shikiriza.org/journee-internationale-de-lacces-a-linformation-ou-en-est-le-burundi/>). [The Senate adopted it unanimously on 29 September 2026](<https://www.burunditimes.com/burundi-adopts-right-to-information-law-with-broad-exceptions/>). No promulgation has been found, and no access to information law in force. Establishing would need an access to information law in force that gives a right to ask public bodies for information.

Benin's access provisions sit in Loi n° 2015-07, the Code de l'information et de la communication of 2015. The World Bank's [December 2022 open data readiness assessment](<https://opendatatoolkit.worldbank.org/content/dam/sites/data/odk/documents/odra-benin.pdf>) calls them extremely limited. [Benin's government told UNESCO, in a return published in October 2024](<https://www.unesco.org/sites/default/files/medias/fichiers/2024/10/Benin_SDG16102_2023.pdf>), that three bodies oversaw the law in 2022, and that they received 12 appeals that year. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decision or count of requests since 2022 has been found. Mature would need a decision, order or penalty, or published figures of requests or complaints, within the past three years.

Burkina Faso's law is [Law no. 051-2015/CNT on the right of access to public information and administrative documents](<https://www.unesco.org/sites/default/files/medias/fichiers/2024/11/BurkinaFaso_SDG16102_2024.pdf>), which the government named to UNESCO as its legal guarantee for 2023. It told UNESCO that existing bodies oversee the law, and that in 2023 they published an annual report and kept statistics on requests and appeals. [A digital rights report of February 2025](<https://burkina24.com/2025/02/11/droits-numeriques-au-burkina-faso-le-centre-national-de-presse-norbert-zongo-presente-son-rapport-2024/>) says the law has fallen into oblivion and names no repeal. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decision, order or penalty on a request, and no published figures, has been found for the last three years. Mature would need one of them.

Botswana's law is [the Access to Information Act, Act 16 of 2024, dated 26 July 2024](<https://botswanalaws.com/consolidated-statutes/acts-on-notice/2024/access-to-information-act>). It creates a general right of access to information held by public authorities and starts on a date to be set by notice. [The President's State of the Nation Address in November 2025 counted the Act among the laws Parliament had passed](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/89031>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. The start date has not been found. No source found names rules made under the Act or says its oversight body is set up. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under it, or an oversight body set up.

Côte d'Ivoire's law is [Law no. 2013-867 of 23 December 2013 on access to information of public interest](<https://data.gouv.ci/pages/open-data>). [The commission that oversees it, the CAIDP, was created in 2013](<https://www.bilan.gouv.ci/uploads/thematiques/175877989036.pdf>), and [recorded 45 referrals in 2024, 12 of them from journalists](<https://pressecotedivoire.fr/22339-acces-a-linformation-publique-lanp-forme-les-journalistes-a-mieux-exercer-leur-droit>). In the last twelve months, [six new commissioners took office on 9 November 2026](<https://www.aip.ci/cote-divoire-aip-six-nouveaux-commissaires-prennent-fonction-a-la-caidp/>). [In September 2026 the commission began a national register of public documents with about 200 information officers](<https://www.fratmat.info/article/2644667/culture/acces-a-linformation-et-aux-documents-publics-la-caidp-engage-le-chantier-du-referentiel-des-documents-publics>).

Cameroon has a draft and no law. [A draft law on the right of access to and use of public information and on the digital transformation of the administration was published on 22 May 2023](<https://www.minpostel.gov.cm/images/Documentation/patnuc/textes_preparation_pour_consultation_publique/e-Government/230519_Loi%20EadmOpendata%20FIN_CLEAN.pdf>). [A national workshop at Ebolowa on 3 to 14 November 2025 gave the draft its technical validation](<https://www.droitmediasfinance.com/index.php/actualites/droit-tech-fintech/1182-cameroun-la-legislation-sur-e-government-facilitant-lacces-a-linformation-publique-au-stade-de-la-validation-officielle>). No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no source found says the draft has reached parliament. Establishing would need an access to information law in force, however old, that gives a right to ask public bodies for information.

[On 27 March 2026 the National Assembly of the Democratic Republic of the Congo declared receivable a private member's bill on access to information](<https://actualite.cd/2026/03/28/assemblee-nationale-la-proposition-de-loi-sur-lacces-linformation-et-la-transparence-de>). It sent the bill to a joint committee with ten days to report. In the last twelve months, [the Congolese press agency reported on 28 September 2026 that three committees were still working on it](<https://acp.cd/nation/rdc-le-projet-de-loi-sur-lacces-a-linformation-p-ublique-vise-aconsolider-la-democratie-linitiateur/>). The bill was to return to plenary afterwards. No access to information law in force has been found. Establishing would need an access to information law in force that gives a right to ask public bodies for information.

The Republic of the Congo has no access to information law and no draft of one. [UNESCO's assessment of the country's internet development, dated 2025, recommends that the government draft and adopt a freedom of information law](<https://www.unesco.org/fr/articles/evaluation-du-developpement-de-linternet-en-republique-du-congo>). It lists a commission on access to public information among the bodies still to be set up. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The assessment names no bill in preparation. Preparing would need a bill or draft to exist: published, validated, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

The Comoros has no access to information law and no draft of one. [UNESCO's contribution to the country's Universal Periodic Review, published in January 2026, states that no access to information law has been adopted](<https://upr-info.org/sites/default/files/country-document/2026-01/UNESCO_org_UPR46_COM_E_Main.pdf>). The contribution names no bill in preparation, in cabinet or before the Assembly of the Union. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a bill or draft to exist: published, validated, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

Cabo Verde's law is [Law no. 10/X/2022 on access to and reuse of administrative documents](<https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/Download/4230>). It was approved on 8 April 2022, promulgated on 9 May 2022 and published on 16 May 2022. It gives everyone a right to consult and copy administrative documents. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names rules made under the law or says its oversight body is set up. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under it, or an information commission or commissioner set up.

Djibouti has a draft and no law found. The Council of Ministers, chaired by the head of state, [examined and approved a draft law on the Digital Code](<https://diplomatie.gouv.dj/Articles/DetailArticles/850>) in June 2023. Book VII of the draft provides a general right of access to administrative documents and public information, and sets rules on how the right is exercised. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the draft was passed. Establishing would need an access to information law in force, however old, that gives a right to ask public bodies for information.

Algeria has no access to information law. [A 2025 thesis at Souk Ahras University says the law called for by the constitutional right of 2016 is still absent](<https://dspace.univ-soukahras.dz/items/68f7c21e-45fe-462c-9afb-5b78ddea0dda/full>). [ARTICLE 19 said in September 2025 that Algeria has no effective right to information legislation, despite years of discussion of draft laws](<https://www.article19.org/resources/mena-setbacks-and-persistent-challenges-to-the-right-to-information/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Neither source names a bill or a published draft. Preparing would need a bill or draft to exist: published, validated, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

[A freedom of information bill backed by the Journalists Syndicate was submitted to Egypt's House of Representatives on 9 August 2026](<https://manassa.news/en/news/33330>) with the signatures of 60 members. It would create an Authority for the Protection of Freedom of Information. [Its explanatory memorandum says the right in Article 68 of the constitution has had no law for years](<https://www.masrawy.com/news/news_egypt/details/2026/8/9/3030353/>). In the last twelve months, the bill is the only step found. No access to information law in force has been found. Establishing would need an access to information law in force, however old, that gives a right to ask public bodies for information.

Eritrea has no access to information law and no draft of one. [UNESCO's contribution to the country's Universal Periodic Review, published in January 2026, states that no freedom of information law has been adopted and recommends that the government introduce one](<https://upr-info.org/sites/default/files/country-document/2026-01/UNESCO_org_UPR46_ERI_E_Main.pdf>). The contribution names no bill in preparation. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a bill or draft to exist: published, validated, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

Ethiopia's law is [Proclamation No. 590/2008](<https://justice.gov.et/en/law/a-proclamation-to-provide-for-freedom-of-the-mass-media-and-access-to-information/>) on Freedom of the Mass Media and Access to Information, dated 4 December 2008. [In December 2025 Birr Metrics reported that a draft to replace it was with the Ministry of Justice](<https://birrmetrics.com/draft-transparency-law-circulates-for-seven-years-still-no-government-approval/>). In the last twelve months, [the House of Peoples' Representatives passed a Freedom of Information Proclamation unanimously on 25 June 2026](<https://ethiopiainsider.com/2026/18375/>). Nothing found says it has been published. Nothing found names rules made under the 2008 proclamation. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law, or its oversight body set up.

Gabon has no access to information law and no draft of one. [UNESCO's contribution to the country's Universal Periodic Review, published in December 2025, states that Gabon has no access to information law and encourages it to adopt one](<https://upr-info.org/sites/default/files/country-document/2025-12/UNESCO_org_UPR42_GAB_F_Main.pdf>). The contribution names no bill in preparation, in cabinet or before parliament. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a bill or draft to exist: published, validated, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

Ghana's law is [the Right to Information Act, 2019 (Act 989)](<https://gna.org.gh/2026/09/rti-act-public-institutions-urged-to-provide-accurate-timely-information-to-citizens/>). The Right to Information Commission oversees and enforces it. [On 5 February 2026 the Commission fined four public institutions GH₵220,000 in total after hearings and determinations](<https://rtic.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/RTIC-IMPOSES-FINES-AND-DIRECTIVE.pdf>). [Its technical advisor reports 819 applications for information in 2025 and 119 applications for review](<https://www.graphic.com.gh/features/opinion/ghana-news-right-to-information-commission-at-six.html>). In the last twelve months, [on 5 August 2026 it imposed penalties of GHS 20,000 each on 254 public institutions](<https://www.graphic.com.gh/news/general-news/upsa-37-military-hospital-among-254-public-institutions-fined-by-rti-commission-over-report-delays.html>) that had not filed their 2025 annual reports under the Act.

Guinea's law is [Law no. 2020/0027/AN on the right of access to public information, signed in Conakry on 19 December 2020](<https://assembleeguinee.org/ndeg-20200027-portant-droit-dacces-linformation-publique-en-republique-de-guinee>). It is in effect from its promulgation and provides for an autonomous commission on access to public information. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The appointment of the commission's members has not been found. No source found names rules made under the law. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under it, or an information commission or commissioner appointed.

The Gambia's law is the Access to Information Act, 2021, which [the Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act of 2025 cites as Act No. 10 of 2021](<https://media2.mofo.com/v3/assets/blt5775cc69c999c255/blt7a10e6071e9d3fad/69d554b553df724b615c685d/personal-data-protection-and-privacy-act-2025.pdf>). [Its chairperson said in October 2025 that the Information Commission had received 15 complaints since its establishment](<https://foroyaa.net/access-to-information-key-to-combating-misinformation-information-commission-chairperson/>), and that draft regulations were with the Ministry of Justice. In the last twelve months, [the Commission, with a deputy chairperson, was implementing the Act in September 2026](<https://thepoint.gm/africa/gambia/national-news/information-commission-trains-csos-on-access-to-information-data-protection>). [A United Nations agency tendered in August 2026 for a communication strategy for it](<https://gambia.unfpa.org/en/vacancies/development-communication-strategy-information-commission-gambia>). No decision, order or penalty on a request has been found.

Guinea-Bissau has a draft and no law. [A drafting commission met on 17 to 23 April 2024 and all those taking part validated the draft law on access to information](<https://www.unesco.org/fr/articles/guinee-bissau-validation-du-projet-de-loi-sur-lacces-linformation>), by UNESCO's account. The next step it gives is submission to the Ministry of Justice for adoption. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says an access to information law is in force. Establishing would need an access to information law in force, however old, that gives a right to ask public bodies for information.

Equatorial Guinea has a bill passed by the Senate and not shown as promulgated. It is for a Code of Transparency, Access to Public Information and Good Governance in Public Finance Management. In the last twelve months, [the Prime Minister presented the bill to the Chamber of Deputies on 5 February 2026](<https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/comparecencia_de_osa_nsue_ante_el_pleno_de_la_camara_de_los_diputados>), and [the Senate approved it unanimously on 8 May 2026](<https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/pleno_de_aprobacion_de_los_proyectos_de_ley_de_transparencia_y_zonas_economicas>). No source found reports promulgation by the Head of State. Establishing would need an access to information law in force, however old, that gives a right to ask public bodies for information.

Kenya's law is the Access to Information Act, 2016, which [gives effect to Article 35 of the Constitution](<https://www.the-star.co.ke/news/2026-09-27-state-vows-proactive-disclosure-as-kenya-marks-access-to-information-day>). The Act [gives oversight and enforcement to the Commission on Administrative Justice](<https://www.rti-rating.org/wp-content/uploads/Kenya.pdf>). [On 16 June 2025 the commission ordered the Kenya Institute of Management to release records a former employee had requested under the Act](<https://www.ombudsman.go.ke/kenya-institute-management-complies-commissions-orders-releases-requested-information>). In the last twelve months, [in August 2026 the commission said it would engage 54 public institutions on compliance](<https://kahawatungu.com/ombudsman-raises-alarm-over-delays-in-resolving-public-complaints/>). It said many do not routinely publish what the Act requires.

Liberia's law is [the Freedom of Information Act of 2010](<https://gnnliberia.com/iic-cental-step-up-transparency-anti-corruption-drive/>). In the last twelve months, [the Independent Information Commission ran a compliance campaign across public bodies from 11 August to 2 September 2026](<https://gnnliberia.com/iic-cental-step-up-transparency-anti-corruption-drive/>). [In October 2026 it ordered the Environmental Protection Agency to give The DayLight newspaper the records it had requested](<https://allafrica.com/stories/202610130246.html>) and fined the agency L$9,000. [The Press Union said in October 2026 that the Commission had publicly opposed the Civil Service Agency's new confidentiality policy](<https://liberiapublicradio.com/2026/10/24/pul-condemns-governments-assault-on-freedom-of-information-and-transparency-calls-for-immediate-withdrawal-of-confidentiality-policy-undermining-the-foi-act/>).

Libya has a draft and no law. [A Council of Ministers draft bill on the national information system, issued on 8 October 2022 over the Prime Minister's signature, would give every citizen a right to request information from the information units of public bodies](<https://lawsociety.ly/legislation/%D9%85%D8%B4%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%B9-%D9%85%D8%B3%D9%88%D8%AF%D8%A9-%D9%82%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%A8%D8%B4%D8%A3%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%86%D8%B8%D8%A7%D9%85-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%88%D8%B7%D9%86%D9%8A-%D9%84/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Its passage has not been found. No source found says an access to information law is in force. Establishing would need an access to information law in force, however old, that gives a right to ask public bodies for information.

Lesotho has an old bill and no law. [An assessment of September 2021](<https://pub.sbc4d.com/2022/lesotho_full_final.pdf>) says the country has no real freedom of information law. It says Parliament has not passed the Access and Receipt of Information Bill of 2000, drafted by the Law Reform Commission. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing later on the bill has been found. Establishing would need an access to information law in force that gives a right to ask public bodies for information.

Morocco's law is [Law no. 31-13 on the right of access to information](<https://www.oc.gov.ma/sites/default/files/loi%2031-13/1.%20BO%20Loi%2031.13%20en%20francais.pdf>), promulgated on 22 February 2018 and published on 3 May 2018. It came into force one year after publication. In the last twelve months, [the Commission on the Right of Access to Information signed a partnership agreement with the Minister of Justice on 31 March 2026](<https://justice.gov.ma/2026/03/31/%D8%AA%D9%88%D9%82%D9%8A%D8%B9-%D8%A7%D8%AA%D9%81%D8%A7%D9%82%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%B6%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%85-%D9%88%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%AF%D9%84-%D8%A5%D9%84%D9%89-%D8%A7/>). The Commission runs the national portal through which requests are made. No decision, order or penalty on a request, and no published figures of requests, has been found for the last three years. Mature would need one of them.

Madagascar has a bill and no law. [A decree of the Prime Minister presented bill no. 017/2025 on access to information of a public nature, in 88 articles](<https://pub-7e0d3a35c1b949698a7ced344fa56252.r2.dev/textes/017-2025/PROJET_LAICP___PR_SENT_E_AU.PDF>). The Council of Ministers had deliberated it on 3 December 2025. In the last twelve months, [deputies debated it in committee from 8 May 2026](<https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique/20260511-madagascar-l%C3%A9gislative-projet-loi-information-%C3%A0-caract%C3%A8re-public>), and [it was left off the agenda of the extraordinary session opened on 25 August 2026](<https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique/20260827-madagascar-une-session-extraordinaire-de-l-assembl%C3%A9e-nationale-sans-le-projet-de-loi-sur-l-information-publique>). No source found says the bill has passed. Establishing would need an access to information law in force, however old, that gives a right to ask public bodies for information.

Mali has no single access to information law. [A study published in April 2026 finds the legal framework for the right spread across several laws](<https://www.revue-irs.com/index.php/home/article/view/1637>), among them Law no. 98-012 on relations between the administration and its users. The study calls for a specific law and names no draft of one. No change to those laws has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names rules made under them or says an oversight body is set up. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law, or an information commission or commissioner set up.

Mozambique's law is [Law no. 34/2014 of 31 December 2014, the Right to Information Law](<https://cscs.gov.mz/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Lei-de-Direito-a-Informacao.pdf>). [The Ombudsman's annual report to the Assembly, reported in November 2025, says public bodies received 60,433 requests for information in 2024](<https://cartamz.com/destaque/47502/provedor-de-justica-garante-haver-melhorias-na-implementacao-da-lei-do-direito-a-informacao/>). Of these, 57,998 were granted, 1,589 refused and 846 still pending, against 23,808 requests in 2023. By the deadline of 30 December 2024, only Manica and Maputo provinces had sent their implementation reports. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says rules have been made under the law.

[Reporters Without Borders reported on 23 June 2026 that a bill drafted by the government on access to and use of public information had been under discussion since April 2026](<https://rsf.org/fr/mauritanie-rsf-salue-le-projet-de-loi-sur-l-acces-et-l-utilisation-de-l-information-publique>). The bill had yet to go through parliament. In the last twelve months, this report is the only step found. No access to information law in force has been found for Mauritania. Establishing would need an access to information law in force, however old, that gives a right to ask public bodies for information.

Mauritius has no access to information law. [On 28 October 2025 the Prime Minister told parliament that exploratory drafting of a bill had begun](<https://lexpress.mu/s/le-freedom-of-information-bil-en-preparation-551179>), and said an older bill was under review. [A Defi Media blog of 14 February 2026 says successive political parties have promised Freedom of Information and failed to deliver](<https://defimedia.info/blog-enough-promises-rama-valayden-urges-action-freedom-information-unveils-proposed-constitutional>). In the last twelve months, [Defimedia reported in November 2026 that the Act promised in the 2025-2029 programme had not been delivered](<https://defimedia.info/programme-2025-2029-ces-grandes-promesses-pas-encore-tenues>). No access to information bill has been found before cabinet or parliament. Preparing would need a bill or draft to exist: published, validated, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

Malawi's law is [the Access to Information Act, 2016, assented to on 10 February 2017 and published in the Gazette on 16 February 2017](<https://malawilii.org/akn/mw/act/2017/13/eng@2017-02-16>). [It became operational on 30 September 2020](<https://www.maraviexpress.com/access-to-information-act-applies-to-private-companies-undertaking-malawi-government-contracts-rules-the-high-court/>). [The Malawi Human Rights Commission, its oversight body, presented a report on carrying out the Act on 10 October 2025](<https://africabrief.substack.com/p/malawi-advances-information-access>). The report says that from April 2024 to March 2025 information holders handled over 36,000 requests and rejected 11. In the last twelve months, the Commission's notice to the company Mota-Engil, to assess whether it could comply, [reached the High Court on 6 March 2026](<https://www.maraviexpress.com/access-to-information-act-applies-to-private-companies-undertaking-malawi-government-contracts-rules-the-high-court/>).

Namibia's law is [the Access to Information Act, 2022 (Act No. 8 of 2022)](<http://www.lac.org.na/laws/2022/7986.pdf>), published on 28 December 2022. It starts on a date the Minister sets by notice. [Regulations made under it were gazetted on 9 December 2024](<https://www.lac.org.na/laws/2024/8530.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [a gazette notice of February 2026 invited applications for Information Commissioner and deputy](<https://www.lac.org.na/laws/2026/8846.pdf>). [By a letter of 27 February 2026 the minister asked the National Assembly to halt the recruitment](<https://www.namibian.com.na/minister-halts-commissioner-recruitment/>). [In May 2026 the African Media Barometer's rapporteur wrote that the Act remains inoperative](<https://www.namibian.com.na/namibias-press-freedom-reputation-is-realbut-the-fine-print-tells-a-different-story/>). No commencement notice has been found. No decision on a request and no published figures of requests have been found. Mature would need a decision, order or penalty, or published figures of requests or complaints.

Niger's law is [Ordinance no. 2011-22 of 23 February 2011 on the charter of access to public information and administrative documents](<https://cyrilla.org/api/files/1566209433658g62junbhzjn.pdf>). [The Minister of Communication cited it on 22 October 2025 as standing](<https://anp.ne/le-niger-veut-se-doter-dune-politique-de-communication-et-dune-strategie-nationale-de-lutte-contre-la-desinformation/>). [Transparency International's Niger chapter said on 10 November 2025 that the ordinance's implementing decree had still not been adopted](<https://transparencyniger.org/?p=243>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says an oversight body is set up. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law, or an information commission or commissioner set up.

Nigeria's law is [the Freedom of Information Act, 2011, assented to on 28 May 2011](<https://nimasa.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/freedom-of-information-act.pdf>). [On 13 October 2025 the Federal High Court in Abuja held the national oil company a public institution under the Act](<http://saharareporters.com/sites/default/files/2026-01/12.%20Judgment%20%28HEDA%20v.%20NNPCL%29-min.pdf>). It ordered the company to supply information requested on a $3 billion loan. In the last twelve months, [on 24 February 2026 the Federal High Court in Lagos ruled that the Nigeria Shippers Council had breached the Act](<https://mediarightsagenda.org/federal-high-court-rules-that-foi-act-overrides-other-laws-in-journalists-suit-against-nigeria-shippers-council/>). The request was a journalist's of 2020. [The Ministry of Justice collects the annual reports the Act requires](<https://www.opengovpartnership.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Nigeria_Action-Plan-Review_2026-2029_For-Public-Comment.pdf>). In 2025, 180 bodies filed none and 61 processed requests, down from 102 in 2024.

Rwanda's law is [Law no. 04/2013 of 8 February 2013 relating to access to information, published on 11 March 2013](<https://rwandalii.org/akn/rw/act/law/2013/4/eng@2013-03-11/source>). In the last twelve months, [ARTICLE 19 told a Universal Periodic Review session on 27 November 2025 that no independent body oversees the law](<https://upr-info.org/sites/default/files/country-document/2025-12/Rwanda_Article_19_statement.pdf>). It said the Ombudsman's access to information mandate had been removed. No source found names rules made under the law. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law, or an information commission or commissioner set up, or an existing body taking up the oversight.

Sudan's law is [the Right to Access Information Law of 2015](<https://cyrilla.org/api/files/1566991640451x872tchicz.pdf>), in effect from signing. The National Assembly ratified it on 27 January 2015 and the President signed it on 22 February 2015. In the last twelve months, [an opinion piece said on 27 November 2025 that the Act's general information commission is still absent](<https://sudafax.com/516941/%d9%82%d8%a7%d9%86%d9%88%d9%86-%d8%ad%d9%82-%d8%a7%d9%84%d8%ad%d8%b5%d9%88%d9%84-%d8%b9%d9%84%d9%89-%d8%a7%d9%84%d9%85%d8%b9%d9%84%d9%88%d9%85%d8%a7%d8%aa-%d9%88%d8%a7%d9%84%d9%85%d9%81%d9%88%d8%b6>). No source found names rules made under the law. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under it, or an information commission or commissioner set up, or an existing body taking up the oversight.

Senegal's law is [Law no. 2025-15 on access to information](<https://www.archives.sn/api/fichiers/e05027c9-f6f2-4f70-a313-b0ee81cf2c08>). It was adopted on 26 August 2025, promulgated on 4 September 2025 and published on 25 September 2025. [The decree on the Commission nationale d'accès à l'information was signed in October 2025](<https://www.ouestaf.com/senegal-acces-a-linformation-la-loi-votee-peu-deffet/>). [Implementing decree no. 2025-1837 requires a complaint to the commission before any court action](<https://www.seneweb.com/fr/news/Justice/la-conai-toujours-pas-installee-un-an-apres-son-adoption-un-blocage-juridique-concret-selon-el-amath-thiam_n_500254.html>). In the last twelve months, [Justice Sans Frontière said on 3 August 2026 that neither the commission's president nor its twelve members had been appointed](<https://www.seneweb.com/fr/news/Justice/la-conai-toujours-pas-installee-un-an-apres-son-adoption-un-blocage-juridique-concret-selon-el-amath-thiam_n_500254.html>). [Ordinance no. 11/2026 of 16 April 2026 declared a request inadmissible](<https://www.vie-publique.sn/documents/11628/ordonnance-11-2026-cour-supreme-rejet-requete-fonds-politiques-2025-2026>), because the applicant had not first gone to the commission. Mature would need a decision, order or penalty, or published figures of requests or complaints.

Sierra Leone's law is [the Right to Access Information Act, 2013](<https://raic.gov.sl/images/downloads/Right-access-information-act-2013.pdf>), signed on 31 October 2013. [On 13 October 2025 the Right to Access Information Commission fined Freetown City Council Le 70,000](<https://www.raic.gov.sl/index.php/all-categories-list/news/raic-fines-freetown-city-council-le-70-000-for-failing-to-release-information>). It ordered the council to release documents within seven days. [A Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill was validated on 7 November 2025](<https://moice.gov.sl/moice-concludes-final-national-validation-of-the-data-protection-and-right-to-access-information-bill-2025/>). In the last twelve months, [Cabinet approved repealing the 2013 Act for the new law, announced on 21 April 2026](<https://moice.gov.sl/cabinet-approves-first-ever-data-protection-policy-paving-way-for-new-data-law/>). [On 12 November 2026 Parliament passed the bill at second reading](<https://sierraleoneconcordtimes.com/parliament-commits-data-protection-bill-to-legislative-committee-by-jariatu-s-bangura/>). [On 23 November 2026 CHRDI sent the Legislative Committee a memorandum](<https://thecalabashnewspaper.com/archives/66364>). It notes that section 92(1) would repeal the 2013 Act.

Somalia has a bill and no law. [The Council of Ministers approved the Official Information Bill in March 2024 and sent it to the House of the People](<https://defenddefenders.org/federal-republic-of-somalia-joint-submission-to-the-un-universal-periodic-review-52nd-session-of-the-upr-working-group/>). [A Ministry of Information official said on 28 September 2025 that the Cabinet had passed the access to information law and that it awaited presentation to the Lower House](<https://soma.org.so/soma-commemorates-international-day-for-universal-access-to-information/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says an access to information law is in force. Establishing would need an access to information law in force, however old, that gives a right to ask public bodies for information.

South Sudan's law is [the Right of Access to Information Act, 2013](<https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/ssd182371.pdf>), in force from the President's assent. It sets up an Information Commissioner. [The budget performance report for 2024/25 lists the Access for Information Commission among the agencies with an allocation](<https://mofp.gov.ss/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/2024_25_Execution-Report_v3.pdf>). [On 4 September 2025 the Ministry of Information said it had estimated a budget for the Commission's operations](<https://mictps.gov.ss/moictps-settles-usaf-information-commission-operation-challenges/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decision, order or penalty on a request, and no published figures of requests, has been found since October 2023. Mature would need one of them.

Sao Tome and Principe has draft bills and no law. [In 2018 civil society organisations submitted a draft Lei de Acesso aos Documentos e Informações Administrativas to the President of the National Assembly](<https://stpdigital.net/sociedade/lei-de-acesso-a-documentos-e-informacoes-administrativas>). [CIPSTP presented its draft access to information bill to the Justice Minister on 8 September 2025](<https://cipstp.st/cipstp-em-audiencia-com-a-ministra-da-justica/>). [UNESCO's contribution of 2026 states that there is no legislation on freedom of information](<https://upr-info.org/sites/default/files/country-document/2026-02/UNESCO_org_UPR51_STP_E_Main.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [Radio Nacional reported in October 2026 that the draft had still not been approved](<https://rstp.st/2026/10/27/profissionais-lamentam-nao-aprovacao-da-lei-de-acesso-a-informacao-em-stp/>). Establishing would need an access to information law in force, however old, that gives a right to ask public bodies for information.

Seychelles' law is [the Access to Information Act, enacted on 20 July 2018](<https://www.infocom.sc/wp-content/uploads/ATIA-Updated-Whitepaper-10.11.2025.pdf>). [The Information Commission was created under it](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-seychelles-dpa>). [In a notice of May 2024 it found the Planning Authority non-compliant with sections 11 and 17](<https://www.infocom.sc/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/17.-Decision-Notice-Ms.-Karen-Domingue-v.-Seychelles-Planning-Authority.pdf>) and ordered full access to the requested files within five days. [It found the Agriculture Department in breach, closing that case on 15 November 2024](<https://www.infocom.sc/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20.-Decision-Notice-Ms.-Rassool-v.-Agriculture-Department-002-002.pdf>). No change to the Act has been found in the last twelve months. The Commission's paper of November 2025 says information holders have ignored its orders and that the Act gives no clear way to enforce them.

Chad has a bill and no law. [The Union of Chadian Journalists said in September 2024 that it had filed a bill on journalists' safety and access to information](<https://www.tachad.com/journee-internationale-de-lacces-a-linformation-lujt-propose-une-loi-pour-proteger-les-journalistes/>). In the last twelve months, [its president said on 28 September 2026 that the bill was still at the National Assembly](<https://tchadinfos.com/2026/09/28/journee-internationale-de-lacces-a-linformation-dans-les-institutions-publiques-il-est-difficile-aujourdhui-davoir-une-information-abbas-mahamoud/>). [A civic-space snapshot of July 2026 states that Chad has no law on access to information](<https://eusee.hivos.org/assets/2026/10/Final-Tchad-2026-Snapshot-_ED-2.pdf>). The bill's text has not been found. Establishing would need an access to information law in force, however old, that gives a right to ask public bodies for information.

Togo's law is [Law no. 2016-006 of 30 March 2016 on freedom of access to public information and documentation](<https://www.rti-rating.org/wp-content/uploads/Togo.pdf>). [Decree no. 2017-104/PR of 10 August 2017 applies it, naming the public bodies it covers and the officials responsible](<https://jo.gouv.tg/sites/default/files/JO/JOS_10_08_2017-62e%20ANNEE%20N%C2%B0%2023%20ter.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decision, order or penalty on a request, and no published figures of requests, has been found for the last three years. Mature would need a decision, order or penalty, or published figures of requests or complaints, within the past three years.

Tunisia's law is [Organic Law no. 22 of 2016 on the right of access to information](<https://inai.tn/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/loi-22-inai.pdf>), promulgated on 24 March 2016. [The government's 2024 return to UNESCO](<https://www.unesco.org/sites/default/files/medias/fichiers/2024/11/Tunisia_SDG16102_2024.pdf>) reports 7,347 appeals received in 2023. [ARTICLE 19 said on 28 August 2025 that the government had ordered the oversight body's activities halted and its seat closed](<https://www.article19.org/ar/resources/tunisia-democracy-at-risk-as-access-to-information-authority-is-dissolved/>). In the last twelve months, [the government told a deputy, as reported on 30 November 2025, that the body has been working without its president and deputy](<https://www.lapresse.tn/2025/12/01/donnees-personnelles-et-acces-a-linformation-lexecutif-engage-une-mise-a-jour-urgente-du-cadre-juridique/>). No decision of the body since 2023 has been found.

Tanzania's law is [the Access to Information Act, 2016](<https://tanzlii.org/akn/tz/act/2016/6/eng@2016-09-30>). It was assented to on 23 September 2016, gazetted on 30 September 2016 and commenced on 1 July 2017. It gives every person a right of access to information held by public bodies. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names rules made under the Act or says its oversight body is set up. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under it, or an information commission or commissioner set up.

Uganda's law is [the Access to Information Act, 2005, assented to on 7 July 2005](<https://www.judiciary.go.ug/files/downloads/access%20to%20informatioinformation%20Act2005.pdf>). [The Africa Freedom of Information Centre says its Regulations of 2011 set out what citizens can request and the exemptions](<https://www.africafoicentre.org/access-to-information-in-uganda-prospects-and-hurdles/>). In the last twelve months, [on 4 December 2025 the Constitutional Court struck down its exemption for court records before a case ends](<https://ulii.org/en/judgments/UGCC/2025/12/>). [On 7 August 2026 the High Court allowed the national examinations board's appeal against a magistrate's order](<https://www.mmaks.co.ug/articles/2026/08/21/examination-scripts-are-personal-data-high-court-sets-aside-order-compelling>) made on a complaint under the Act. The Act sets up no information commission, and no published figures of requests have been found.

South Africa's law is [the Promotion of Access to Information Act of 2000](<https://www.mondaq.com/southafrica/contracts-and-commercial-law/1797238/landmark-ruling-for-private-bodies-under-paia-information-regulators-enforcement-notice-against-mining-house>). [The Information Regulator, established on 1 December 2016](<https://www.itweb.co.za/article/inforeg-unpacks-regulatory-complexities-posed-by-ai/KA3WwMdzPryvrydZ>), enforces it. In the last twelve months, [complaints under the Act could be lodged online from January 2026](<https://www.itweb.co.za/article/inforeg-strengthens-cyber-defences-as-breaches-mount/DZQ58vV8WyPMzXy2>). [On 22 May 2026 the Regulator ordered the mining company Sibanye-Stillwater](<https://www.mondaq.com/southafrica/contracts-and-commercial-law/1797238/landmark-ruling-for-private-bodies-under-paia-information-regulators-enforcement-notice-against-mining-house>) to give a complainant access to compliance reports. [On 16 November 2026 it set aside a public service department's refusal of a request](<https://www.itweb.co.za/article/inforeg-calls-out-dpsa-in-cellphone-allowance-dispute/rW1xL75nkZPMRk6m>). No source found reports how many requests are made under the Act.

Zambia's law is [the Access to Information Act, 2023 (Act No. 24 of 2023)](<https://www.parliament.gov.zm/sites/default/files/documents/acts/Act%20No.%2024%20of%202023%2C%20The%20Access%20to%20Information%20Act%2C%202023.pdf>), assented to on 22 December 2023. [The Human Rights Commission says it came into force on 25 June 2024](<https://hrc.org.zm/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/2026.01.08-HRC-Statement-on-ATI.pdf>). [The Minister made the Access to Information (General) Regulations, 2025, signed on 20 August 2025](<https://zambialii.org/akn/zm/act/si/2025/56/eng@2025-08-29/source>). In the last twelve months, [the Commission, the Act's oversight body, issued guidelines on 5 December 2025](<https://hrc.org.zm/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Access-To-Information-Guidelines_2025.pdf>). [On 23 June 2026 it said it had written to the Ministry of Health directing it to comply with the law on requests from MakanDay](<https://makanday.org/access-denied-two-years-after-zambias-ati-law-citizens-still-struggle-for-public-information/>). No decision or penalty on a request, and no published figures, has been found. Mature would need one of them.

Zimbabwe's law is [the Freedom of Information Act, 2020, published and commenced on 1 July 2020](<https://zimlii.org/akn/zw/act/2020/1/eng@2020-07-01>). [MISA Zimbabwe's 2024 annual report says the Zimbabwe Media Commission has issued release orders to public institutions](<https://zimbabwe.misa.org/2025/04/26/misa-zimbabwe-2024-annual-report-now-available/>). In the last twelve months, [a joint submission to the United Nations of July 2026 says the Act was put to work through the Freedom of Information (General) Regulations, 2021](<https://cipesa.org/wp-content/files/Zimbabwe_UPR_Review.pdf>). It recommends that the Act be fully carried out. No count or date of the Commission's release orders has been found.
